name: Jamāl al-Dīn Abū ʿAmr ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Ḥājib
summary: Mālikī jurist and grammarian, author of al-Kāfiya on naḥw and al-Shāfiya on ṣarf, the two short handbooks behind much of the Indian and Ottoman curriculum.
bio: Ibn al-Ḥājib was born in Upper Egypt and studied in Cairo. He taught in Cairo and then in the Great Mosque of Damascus, left Damascus after a dispute with its Ayyubid ruler, and died in Alexandria in 646/1249.
He wrote in grammar, law and uṣūl al-fiqh. His al-Kāfiya (syntax) and al-Shāfiya (morphology) were read and commented on for centuries, from Cairo to Istanbul and Delhi.
